Planning services

How much planning help do you actually need?

Australian planners sell their work at three levels: full planning, partial planning and on-the-day coordination. The level you pick moves the price more than the planner you pick does, so it is worth settling before you enquire.

Get event planning quotesFind a planner
  • Three levels, compared line by line
  • Weddings, parties and functions
  • Free to enquire

Start here

How do you know which level you need?

Answer one question honestly: how much of this can you carry between now and the event?

Full planning

Pick full planning when almost nothing is booked and the hours do not exist. A useful test: if you cannot name three suppliers you already want, this is your level.

Engaged nine to fourteen months out for a wedding, three to six for most other events.

  • The brief, the concept and the budget frame
  • Venue shortlist, site visits and contract review
  • Every supplier sourced, quoted and booked
  • One budget, held and reconciled
  • Run sheet, supplier briefing and the day itself

Partial planning

Pick partial planning when the venue and date are locked in and the middle of your list has stopped moving. You keep the decisions you enjoy. Your planner takes the ones sitting open.

Engaged four to eight months out. The level most people should buy and do not.

  • Starts from wherever you have got to
  • Shortlists for the suppliers still missing
  • Timeline and budget pulled into one place
  • Styling resolved against what is already booked
  • Coordination on the day, in most packages

On-the-day coordination

Pick coordination when the plan is finished and you do not want to be the person every supplier rings. Nothing you booked changes. Somebody else becomes the contact.

Engaged two to three months out, with the handover four to six weeks before.

  • Full handover of everything you built
  • Every supplier confirmed and briefed
  • One run sheet, circulated to all of them
  • On-site management, bump in to bump out
  • You attend your own event as a guest

Side by side

What actually changes between the three levels?

Package names vary between planners. The scope underneath them is remarkably consistent.

How the three levels differ in scope. Packages vary, so confirm the detail in writing with your planner.

Planner vs coordinator

The exclusions

What is not included at any level?

The boundary is where disputes happen. These five exclusions are close to universal.

The suppliers themselves

A planning fee buys the planner and nothing else. Venue, catering, drinks, flowers and hire are quoted separately, so a $6,000 planning fee sits on top of the event budget, not inside it.

Styling stock and hire items

Planners specify and book decor. They rarely own it. Furniture, props and lighting are billed as hire. Check whether you are buying the booking or the stock.

Unlimited meetings and site visits

Most packages set a number, and two site visits is common. Extras are billable, and for a regional venue they can be the largest variable in the quote.

Travel beyond the service area

Past the edge of a planner's service area, travel and sometimes accommodation is added. Two quotes are not comparable until you know where each boundary sits.

Anything you have not mentioned yet

If the guest list grows by forty, that is a variation. Get it repriced when it happens, not in an argument over the final invoice.

Getting it wrong

What happens if you choose the wrong level?

Almost nobody over-buys. People under-buy, and they find out in the last six weeks, which is the worst possible time. The pattern is consistent: a host books coordination because the plan feels finished, then the coordinator starts confirming suppliers and finds three who were never booked in writing.

Moving up a level part way through is normal. Moving down is harder, because the sourcing work the lower package excludes has usually been done. The other common error is buying a level that does not match the venue: a dry hire site, where you supply everything from the tables to the power, is a full planning job even with a small guest list, as our venue sourcing page explains.

The most common mistake

Buying coordination when the plan is not finished. Coordination assumes a complete, confirmed plan handed over intact. If yours has gaps in it, what you actually need is partial planning with coordination attached, and it is far cheaper to say so at the quote stage than in the final month.

Tell us where your planning is up to

Straight answers

Choosing a planning service

Which planning service is the cheapest?

On-the-day coordination, because it is the smallest scope. Easy Weddings, in a guide updated February 2026, puts a day-of coordinator at roughly $1,500 to $2,000 against $5,000 to $6,000 for full-service planning. It is only good value if your plan is genuinely finished.

Can I start with coordination and upgrade later?

Usually yes. You pay the difference and the scope is rewritten. What you cannot reliably do is upgrade in the last month, because the sourcing work a higher package includes takes time that no longer exists.

Does the planning fee include the cost of the event?

No. A planning fee pays for the planner's time. Venue, catering, drinks, flowers and hire are quoted separately and paid to each supplier. A percentage-based fee is calculated on the event budget but still sits on top of it.

What is partial planning called at other companies?

The names are not standardised in Australia. Partial planning is also sold as planning support or a hybrid package, and on-the-day coordination as day of coordination, month of coordination or wedding day management. Ignore the label and read the inclusion list.

How does an enquiry through this site work?

You tell us what you are planning, roughly when and where, and how much help you want. We pass your enquiry through My Event Match to event planners and coordinators who cover your area and work on your kind of event. Planners reply to you directly, so timing depends on the planner and the season. Free to enquire, and you pay your planner directly.

One enquiry, then it is somebody else's job

Not sure which level you need?

Tell us what you are planning and how much of it is already booked. The enquiry goes to planners who cover your area and work on your kind of event.
